summary: Registers a URN namespace for the Open IPTV Forum, for naming persistent resources defined in its specifications, such as documents, XML schemas, classification schemes and media assets. It is informational.

plainLanguage.summary: A group of TV-over-internet companies gets its own special naming system so their documents and files always have a permanent name.

questions: what is the oipf urn namespace
how are open iptv forum resources named
why does iptv need a namespace
subtitle: A naming system for the Open IPTV Forum specifications.

tldr.problem: The Open IPTV Forum creates many technical documents, XML schemas, and digital assets for IPTV systems. These resources need permanent, location-independent names so they can be referenced reliably in the future.
tldr.mechanism: The document registers a formal URN namespace identifier 'oipf' with IANA. Resources are named using the pattern urn:oipf: followed by a resource-specific identifier, managed and published by the OIPF.
tldr.outcome: The OIPF now has a global, formal namespace for naming its specifications and related resources. This provides stability and a common reference point for implementers.

today: RFC 6893 is an Informational document that establishes a formal URN namespace for the Open IPTV Forum. The namespace remains active and in use for naming IPTV specifications and resources. The registry is published and maintained by the OIPF on its website at oipf.tv.

sections.title: The Open IPTV Forum
sections.content:
IPTV (Internet Protocol Television) brings television and multimedia services over internet networks instead of using traditional broadcast or cable. The Open IPTV Forum is an industry consortium created to develop and standardize end-to-end specifications for IPTV deployments. It includes communications companies, content providers, device manufacturers, and network operators.

The Forum produces comprehensive specifications covering architecture, network functionality, security, user interfaces, device certification, and more. To create a cohesive ecosystem, it also defines many supporting resources: XML schemas, classification schemes, format definitions, namespaces, stylesheets, and media assets. Each of these resources needs a permanent, location-independent name that persists even if the resource moves or is updated.
sections.plainLanguage: Many companies work together to write standards for TV over the internet. They create hundreds of documents and formats, and they need a permanent way to name all of them so everyone can find them later.

sections.title: The URN Namespace Solution
sections.content:
A URN (Uniform Resource Name) is a name for a resource that is independent of where it is located—unlike a URL (Uniform Resource Locator), which includes the address. URNs follow the syntax defined in RFC 2141: urn:<namespace-id>:<namespace-specific-string>.

This document registers a new formal namespace with the namespace identifier (NID) of oipf. Resources in this namespace follow the pattern urn:oipf:<resource-identifier>. The OIPF controls the assignment of all identifiers within this namespace and publishes them through its specifications and website.
sections.plainLanguage: A URN is like a name instead of an address. You can name something 'urn:oipf:mytv-schema-2009' and that name stays the same forever, even if you move it to a different website.

sections.title: How the Namespace Works
sections.content:
The OIPF assigns unique identifiers as it develops its specifications. The organization commits to maintaining the uniqueness and persistence of all assigned URNs. Once a name is assigned, it is never reassigned to a different resource. The OIPF publishes registration tables and information on its website, and examples are drawn from OIPF Release 1 IPTV specifications.

Example OIPF URNs include: urn:oipf:device:ig:1, urn:oipf:config:oitf:oitfCapabilities:2009, and urn:oipf:cs:AVMediaFormatCS:2008. The format is case-insensitive. The namespace is global, meaning the names are recognized and understood anywhere in the world.

URN resolution (looking up what a URN refers to) is not formally configured through a discovery system; instead, implementers consult the OIPF website and the relevant specifications. The assignment and publication processes are fully managed by the OIPF.
sections.plainLanguage: The OIPF gives each resource a permanent name, writes it down, and promises never to reuse the name for anything else. Anyone can look up the name on the OIPF website to find what it refers to.

sections.title: Impact and Scope
sections.content:
Resources identified in the OIPF namespace include XML schema definition files, classification schemes, capability descriptions, and media format specifications. These are the building blocks of the OIPF IPTV Solution. By providing them with stable, formal names, the namespace enables long-term interoperability. Implementers of IPTV systems and services can reference these resources with confidence that the names remain valid and meaningful across product updates and vendor changes.

The namespace applies globally and covers resources produced or managed by the OIPF itself. Security considerations are minimal: the namespace itself does not provide authentication or validation, but the OIPF specifies those concerns in the actual specifications that use the URNs. As with all URN namespaces, security depends on the organization managing the namespace ensuring that assignments are trustworthy and properly documented.
sections.plainLanguage: By giving its specifications and standards permanent names, the OIPF makes it easy for companies all over the world to build compatible IPTV systems. Everyone knows the names will never change, so they can rely on them.
